headline: Gold in toilet
source: Directorate of Revenue Intelligence, via PIB, 25 Jul 2026
captionHeadline: About 12 kg of gold bars, hidden behind the ceiling panels of a plane's rear toilet.
summary: That was one catch on a flight from Addis Ababa. In a single week, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence says it seized 27 kg of smuggled gold, including gold dust hidden in wax, and arrested 12 people.
forYou: The gold flew in. The smuggler didn't have to carry it.
cta: Send this to the friend who always takes forever in the airplane toilet. Follow @postr.news: File #04 drops next.

slides.label: JULY 2026
slides.body: A flight lands in India from *Addis Ababa*. Officers head for the rear toilet.
slides.title: ACTING ON INTELLIGENCE

slides.label: THE CEILING
slides.body: They open the ceiling panels. Inside: *gold bars.*

slides.label: THE WEIGHT
slides.body: About *12 kg* of gold. Hidden where no passenger would ever look.

slides.label: THE TRICK
slides.title: Why hide it in the plane, not a bag
points: A bag gets scanned. A ceiling panel doesn't
Nobody on board has to carry it through customs
The gold waits for someone to collect it later
It's an old trick to stay away from the scanners

slides.label: ALSO THAT WEEK
slides.body: Gold turned into *dust*, mixed into *wax*, so it passes as something else.

slides.label: WHY GOLD
slides.title: Why smugglers love gold
slides.body: Gold is small, valuable and easy to sell for cash anywhere in India. Smuggled in, it skips import duty. Sold for cash, it leaves no paper trail.

slides.label: THE TWIST
slides.body: All this in *one week*. From one agency.

slides.label: NEXT FILE
slides.body: Cash. Liquor. Drugs. Gold. *₹8,889 crore* of it, seized to buy one thing: *your vote.*
slides.title: FILE #04

slides.label: FOLLOW THE FILES
slides.title: Check the ceiling next time

headline: Votes for sale
captionHeadline: ₹8,889 crore. That's what was seized to buy votes before the 2024 Lok Sabha election had even finished.
summary: Cash, liquor, drugs, precious metals and freebies were picked up by enforcement teams by 18 May 2024, with phases still left to vote. Drugs alone made up about 45% of it.
forYou: This is only what got caught.
cta: Send this to the friend who says "my one vote doesn't matter". Someone thought it was worth paying for. Follow @postr.news: File #05 drops next.

slides.label: SPRING 2024
slides.body: India goes to vote. Flying squads start stopping cars on every highway.
slides.title: LOK SABHA ELECTION

slides.label: IN THE BOOTS
slides.body: *Cash.* *Liquor.* Drugs. Gold. Free gifts.

slides.label: BY 18 MAY 2024
slides.body: *₹8,889 crore* seized. With phases still left to vote.

slides.label: WHAT THEY FOUND
slides.title: The price of a vote
points: Cash meant to be handed out
Liquor
Drugs: about 45% of everything seized
Gold, silver and freebies

slides.label: THE SHOCK
slides.body: Almost *half* of it was *drugs.*

slides.label: THE RECORD
slides.title: Bigger than any election before
slides.body: The Election Commission said seizures in 2024 were the highest ever recorded for a Lok Sabha election, even before voting had finished.

slides.label: THE TWIST
slides.body: This is only what *got caught.*

slides.label: THE QUESTION
slides.body: Someone thought your one vote was *worth paying for.*

slides.label: NEXT FILE
slides.body: How *₹100 crore* of drug money crossed a border *without crossing it.*

headline: Narco hawala trail
captionHeadline: A ₹100 crore drug-money trail, running through bank accounts in Mizoram towns and out to suppliers in Myanmar.
summary: The Enforcement Directorate says it froze 1,424 accounts, arrested 18 people, attached ₹17.82 crore and found 500 detonators in its hawala probe. All accused are innocent until proven guilty.
forYou: 1,424 accounts. Most of them in other people's names.
cta: Send this to the friend who binge-watches Narcos. Follow @postr.news: File #06 drops next.

slides.label: MIZORAM
slides.body: Three towns in Mizoram. Ordinary bank accounts. *Not so ordinary money.*
slides.title: THE BORDER

slides.label: THE TRAIL
slides.body: The Enforcement Directorate says *₹100 crore* of drug money moved through them.

slides.label: WHERE IT WENT
slides.body: Out to drug suppliers in *Myanmar.* Through *hawala.*

slides.label: HOW HAWALA WORKS
slides.title: Money that moves without moving
points: You hand cash to an agent on one side
He calls a partner across the border
The partner pays out the same amount there
No bank. No wire. No record. They settle later

slides.label: THE BUST
slides.title: What the ED says it found

slides.label: AND THEN
slides.body: Officers also found *500 detonators.*

slides.label: THE ACCOUNTS
slides.title: 1,424 accounts frozen
slides.body: Drug networks rarely use their own names. They use other people's bank accounts to break the trail. All accused are innocent until proven guilty in court.

slides.label: THE TWIST
slides.body: The money never crossed the border. *The debt did.*

slides.label: NEXT FILE
slides.body: And then there's the most famous hiding place of all: *Swiss banks.* ₹36,793 crore of it.

headline: Swiss bank money
source: Swiss National Bank annual data, released 19 Jun 2026
captionHeadline: ₹36,793 crore. Money linked to India sitting in Swiss banks at the end of 2025.
summary: The total (CHF 3.25 billion) fell 8%, but customer deposits jumped more than 50% to CHF 524 million. Swiss authorities say these figures "cannot be considered as black money": most of it belongs to banks and companies.
forYou: Officially, it's not black money. So whose is it?
cta: Send this to the friend who still says "Swiss account". Follow @postr.news: File #07 drops next.

slides.label: THE MYTH
slides.body: Every Indian has heard it: *"Sab paisa Swiss account mein hai."*
slides.title: EVERY ELECTION

slides.label: THE DATA
slides.body: Every June, the *Swiss National Bank* publishes how much money is linked to India.

slides.label: END OF 2025
slides.body: *₹36,793 crore.* CHF 3.25 billion.

slides.label: THE CATCH
slides.body: The Swiss say this *"cannot be considered as black money".*

slides.label: WHY
slides.title: So whose money is it
slides.body: Most of it sits with banks and Indian companies' branches doing normal business. Switzerland also shares account details with India every year under a global tax deal.

slides.label: THE TWIST
slides.body: The total fell. But money in *customer accounts* jumped more than *50%.*

slides.label: THE QUESTION
slides.body: If the Swiss vault isn't where black money hides anymore, *where did it move?*

slides.label: NEXT FILE
slides.body: Sometimes it's hiding in *your* account. Or your cousin's. *24.67 lakh* of them.
slides.title: FILE #07

slides.label: FOLLOW THE FILES
slides.title: The Swiss account myth

headline: Mule account army
source: Lok Sabha reply on the I4C suspect registry, Dec 2025
captionHeadline: 24.67 lakh bank accounts in India were flagged as "mules", used to move scam money so it can't be traced.
summary: The government's cyber crime centre (I4C) runs a suspect registry with banks. It says the registry has helped block ₹8,031.56 crore. Many mules are ordinary people who "rent out" an account for a small cut.
forYou: The scammer disappears. The account holder is the one the police find.
cta: Send this to the cousin who got a "₹5,000 a month for your account" offer. Follow @postr.news: File #08 drops next.

slides.label: THE OFFER
slides.body: *"₹5,000 a month. Just let us use your bank account."*
slides.title: A TYPICAL OFFER

slides.label: IT SOUNDS EASY
slides.body: You do nothing. Money comes in. Money goes out. *You keep a cut.*

slides.label: WHAT YOU BECAME
slides.body: A *money mule.* The last link in someone else's scam.

slides.label: HOW IT WORKS
slides.title: Your account, their money
points: A scam victim sends money to your account
It's moved out within minutes
It hops through more accounts until it vanishes
Your name is the one left on the trail

slides.label: THE NUMBER
slides.body: *24.67 lakh* accounts. Flagged by the government's cyber crime centre.

slides.label: WHO THEY ARE
slides.title: Mostly ordinary people
slides.body: Often students, gig workers or people who needed a little extra money. Many were told it was a "job". The I4C suspect registry shares these accounts with banks so the money can be frozen.

slides.label: THE TWIST
slides.body: The scammer disappears. *The mule takes the fall.*

slides.label: NEXT FILE
slides.body: At the other end: the very rich, hiding money in *secret companies abroad.* Until the files leaked.
slides.title: FILE #08

headline: Leaked offshore files
source: Government reply in Lok Sabha, 23 Mar 2026
captionHeadline: ₹14,636 crore of hidden foreign income, taxed after the Panama, Paradise and Pandora leaks.
summary: And under the Black Money Act, the tax department raised ₹4,009.64 crore in FY26 (April to December), with 1,368 assessments and 167 prosecutions filed.
forYou: None of it was found by a raid. It was found because someone leaked the files.
cta: Send this to someone who thinks offshore means safe. Follow @postr.news: File #09 drops next.

slides.body: A law firm in *Panama* that kept the world's secrets. Then someone *leaked* them.
slides.title: THE FIRST LEAK

slides.label: 11.5 MILLION FILES
slides.body: Secret companies. Hidden owners. *Indian names among them.*

slides.label: THEN TWO MORE
slides.body: *Paradise Papers*, 2017. *Pandora Papers*, 2021.

slides.label: HOW IT WORKS
slides.title: How money hides offshore
points: Set up a company in a tax haven
Put someone else's name on it as owner
Move money in, out of sight of tax officers
Bring it back as "investment" years later

slides.label: INDIA'S BILL
slides.body: *₹14,636 crore* of hidden foreign income, taxed after the leaks.

slides.label: THE TWIST
slides.body: None of it was found by a raid. It was found because *someone leaked the files.*

slides.label: THE QUESTION
slides.body: How many offshore companies *haven't* leaked yet?

slides.label: NEXT FILE
slides.body: You don't need a tax haven. *17,818* companies existed only on paper. *Right here.*
